utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we continue, I'd like to verify whether the videolink is functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Thank you. Good morning, Your Honours. Yes, we can hear and see you clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can hear and see you as well. Mr. Traldi will now continue his cross-examination, and I inform the parties that in view of the absence of Mr. Mladic that we'll have sessions of one hour and a half and a longer break then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I start this morning if I could just tender the last three documents from yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you remind us which they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the numbers would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 18365 receives number P7328. 18366 receives number P7329. And 12842 receives number P7330.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7328, P7329, and P7330 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, just very briefly there's one translation matter that may arise with a document that I'll use this session. Mr. Stojanovic and I are in agreement about it and I'll just note if it arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before we continue, Mr. Boric, I'd like to remind that you you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to start today with your first meeting with General Mladic in Petrovac. Yesterday, you said he was addressing a meeting there and you testified it was in April 1991. This meeting, in fact, was in April 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at this meeting General Mladic told the assembled leaders in Petrovac municipality, among other things, to prepare for war and for defence; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His words were uttered in that sense, given the fact that he had already seen war in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when he's talking about -- when he was talking about preparing for war, the enemy then would be the Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And once you became corps commander, you would speak with General Mladic every morning; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly every morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, can we have 65 ter 32422, page 90. This is a portion of your suspect interview with the Office of the Prosecutor. And at the end of your first answer, you say: "I would speak to General Mladic every morning between 7.00 and 8.00 a.m. and I would just say, Boss, everything is fine, if it was fine. If it wasn't ..." And then in your next answer, you explain the problems would be included in your report. Do you stand by this portion of your interview with the Office of the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had occasion to speak to him every morning, if needed, but I'm not certain that we actually did speak every morning. Because I wasn't at the command post all the time. I also toured my units, and when possible, I would be in communication with him. In any case, whatever I said, I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not entirely clear from your answer. Is it right that you're adopting now your statement in your interview that you would speak to him every morning between 7.00 and 8.00?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't speak every morning. I can't accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that a number be reserved for portions of the interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you reserve a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the number to reserve is P7331.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and will deal with excerpts from the witness interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And regarding the 2nd Krajina Corps and you yourself, Mladic was always aware of what was going on; right.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You described yesterday the reporting by the 2nd Krajina Corps to the Main Staff. General Mladic would review those reports, and every second or third day, a representative of the Main Staff would be sent to the corps command; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not every second or third day. Not as often. Let's say once or twice every month, and, if needed, it was more frequent. That was the frequency of visits of representatives of the Main Staff to the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32422, page 87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's P7331, reserved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. Yes, P7331.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, beginning in the middle of the page, you were asked: "... every day, you have to know that every day we had to send the report to the Main Staff by 1800 hours of everything that happened in the AOR that day. Based on that, the command of the Main Staff had, used to send his subordinates to visit the corps. And ... they would spend two or three days in the corps and once they were done they'd submit the report to the Main Staff command. So every second or third day, we had a representative, some representative of the Main Staff in the corps." So my first question is: Do you stand by this portion of your interview as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the moment, sir, I'm interested in whether you say so today. Do you stand by this portion of your interview as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that everything is accurate except for the fact that "every day" someone came to the corps from the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, your introduction to the portion you read reads you were asked, but it was not the question, but the response by the person named GB.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And between that and the complete text I may have create add small amount of confusion which I'll try to rectify now, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, "every day" in your previous interview referred to the reporting. What it says here is: "Based on that, the command of the Main Staff had used to send his subordinates to visit the corps and then they would spent two or three days in the corps and once they were done, they'd submit the report to the Main Staff command. So every second or third day, we had a representative, some representative of the Main Staff in the corps." The portion that I have just read out to you now, do you today stand by that as truthful and accurate, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And was that the case throughout the war?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It didn't take place every two or three days. Perhaps every fortnight. It all depended on the situation at the front.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'll ask to include this page in the excerpts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: General Mladic, because of his visits and the Main Staff visits, knew all the brigade commanders and all the brigade commands in your corps; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He knew all the brigade commanders, but I can't say that he knew each and every officer in the brigade commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the combat operations planned by your corps were planned in response to larger directives from the Main Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You'd gather your staff in the operations centre, inform them of the Main Staff's order, and then draft your own order on that basis to send to subordinate units; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And your brigade commanders never launched an offensive operation without your approval that you know of; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is also true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Communications from the Main Staff were sent to your corps' operations centre; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, we're going to pull up one document in Sanction now, 65 ter 23429, and I'd just ask to you say "yes" when you can see it on your screen there.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Mr. Traldi, I'm sorry, we can see the document but it is not legible. The witness cannot read it and we don't have it on the DVD provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It arises out of one answer he provided yesterday. Can we zoom in on the date in the top left corner. I won't be asking him to refer to any text.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you see that the date is the 20th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And turning to the end in both languages, the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we can see the second language, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm told we can only play one in Sanction at a time. And because it's just the dates, Your Honour, that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at the end, we see a receipt stamp from the 10th Corps operations centre. Can you also see the date, the 20th of May, 1992 there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we centralise the stamp.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, at the time the 10th Corps operations stamp would have referred to your operations centre, the one that had previously been the operations centre of the 10th Corps of the JNA; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That stamp that shows it was received by the 10th Corps operations centre on the 20th of May, 1992, that's your operations centre; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the operations centre of the 10th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And at the time, that's your corps; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was then appointed as corps commander to a corps that didn't exist practically speaking. All the units that were in Croatian territory remained there. Only some soldiers and officers, as well as some assets, were pulled out to the territory of Petrovac. At that time I had not been appointed the commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the pull-out to Petrovac was from Bihac, right, as you testified yesterday?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you very simply is yesterday I showed you a document from the VRS Main Staff dated 19th of May. You suggested in your answer that you were not receiving information from the Main Staff until the 23rd. What I'm putting to you is: Your corps was clearly receiving information from the Main Staff the same day it was sent, no later than the 20th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall whether the centre existed in the first place although I see the stamp. We moved out and there was no command in place except for the units which reached the sector of Petrovac. They were the units I commanded. I had no communication with the JNA staff, and there was no communication with the Main Staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 23429.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7332.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is there a translation uploaded, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for -- to know for sure. We haven't seen it yet. But P7332 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, sir, at transcript page 34593, you testified that you didn't know that there was a Crisis Staff in any of the municipalities in your area of responsibility. Now, in your suspect interview, you mentioned that a representative of the VRS always had to be on each municipality's Crisis Staff. First, does that refresh your recollection as to whether you knew such Crisis Staffs existed in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not state that, that there was a VRS representative on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At no municipality was there a representative of the 2nd Krajina Corps ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 32422, page 148, as it comes up, sir, what I'm suggest to that you is a representative at the brigade level was on each municipality's Crisis Staff, not from the corps command. And you were asked here in the middle of the page by Mr. Grady. "We know from investigating many municipal Crisis Staffs and regional Crisis Staffs that it was very common for a commander of the -- of the brigades to be a member of the Crisis Staffs [sic]." You answer: "A representative of the army always had to be there." And he asks you: "Why was that? Was that a policy that was established by the SDS in agreement with the army? And you answer: "No, this was according to our rules, even at peacetime, that these staffs would be attended by -- had to be attended by a representative of the military." Now do you stand by your portion of your interview as truthful and accurate today?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is not accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the very end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, could you repeat your explanation as to why your previous answer was not accurate.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do not interrupt me. Please do not interrupt me. If you're asking me to answer, do not interrupt. There's nothing else to say on my part. It is not true. The commander -- the brigade commander did not have any links with the municipal president. I don't know whether the municipal president would come to the Crisis Staff, but the brigade commander was aware of the issues being worked on at a particular moment in the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that you incorrectly and untruthfully stated 11 years ago that representatives of the army always had to be present at Crisis Staff meetings; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. Could the witness kindly take his earphones off. I'd like to point to an issue in the transcript that was indicated to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that the witness has done so. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 11, sorry. Page 11, line 4, apparently something contradicting what the witness said was entered. What was entered that there was no communication between the brigade commander and the municipal president, whereas the witness said they were always in contact. Which can cause confusion. Perhaps my learned friend, the Prosecutor, could clear this up with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm happy to follow Mr. Stojanovic's suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness put his -- put on his earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, sir, is it correct that you testified a moment ago - and this is just a matter for the transcript - that the brigade commander and the municipal president were always in contact?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. They were in the same territory and they were in contact all the time. Directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, second, just to make sure I understand your answers regarding the relationship between the brigade and the Crisis Staff, it's your evidence today that you inaccurately and untruthfully stated in your interview that a representative of the VRS always had to attend Crisis Staff meetings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see where it is that I stated that. If it is written down, I'd like to see that here. Not a single representative of the army was on the Crisis Staff. Not in a single municipality. And also no representative of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Not in a single municipality. Not in a single Crisis Staff. I firmly stand by that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, it will be read to you again. It is not available in your language, but if need be, we could verify whether this is what you said, because there's an audio recording of this interview. So therefore if you say, I didn't say it, then we'll verify that. And if you -- if it's read again to, if you would say, Yes, I may have said that, please tell us. Could you read again the portion you're focussing on, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Grady asks: "We know from investigating many municipal Crisis Staffs and regional Crisis Staffs that it was very common for a commander of the -- of the brigades to be a member of the Crisis Staff." You respond: "A representative of the army always had to be there." You're then asked: "Why was that? Was that a policy that was established by the SDS in agreement with the army? " You respond: "No. This was according to our rules," you say, "even at peacetime, that these staffs would be attended by -- had to be attended by a representative of the military." So, again, do you say, yes, you may have said? Do you say, I didn't say that? Do you recall making that statement in your OTP interview?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't wish to be cautioned, so, again, could I kindly ask that the witness take off his earphones for a moment. I do apologise to you, General. I would like the Trial Chamber to approve of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, could I just verify with the representative of the Registry in the videolink room, if the witness takes off his earphones, is there any way, he could, nevertheless, hear what Mr. Stojanovic is saying now?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Your Honours, no, there's no way that he can hear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I now object to the question because this is a mis-citation. The transcript does not reflect at all that the witness said that somebody from the brigade was a member of the Crisis Staff. The concept of Crisis Staff was used --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the end of Mr. Stojanovic's answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, what Mr. Traldi read, that is, attending those meetings, is -- I would agree with you, is slightly different from the language used before to be a member of the Crisis Staff. But the way in which the question was phrased is accurate and correct. Therefore, the objection is denied. Could the witness put on his earphones again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I know it's been a moment. Do you recall the portion of your interview that I've now read to you twice?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that in the Crisis Staff it was not obligatory to have a representative of the military. However, when certain meetings were held a representative of the army would be invited and a representative would attend. I allow for that. I allow that I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but could we then go back to the question that was put to you, whether what was read to you, whether that is what you said during the interview.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because you keep telling me that it is obligatory for a member of the military to be on the Crisis Staff, which is not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not putting that to you. I'm asking you whether what was read by Mr. Traldi, read being your words during the interview, whether you acknowledge that you used those words or that you deny or dispute that you used that language when you were interviewed. I'm not asking you at this moment how it was, but I'm asking exclusively on whether that is what you said during the interview. Could you answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stand by what I said just now. I cannot say anything different.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm asking you again: Whether the words read out to you reflects what you said during your interview. Apart from whether you stand by it, but just whether that is what you said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received evidence that, for instance, Bosko Lukic was on the Crisis Staff in Kljuc. He was a member of the 17th Brigade in your corps; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, in view of the previous answer of the witness, the Chamber would appreciate if you, together with the Defence, would verify whether the transcript of the interview is accurate and whether those words were spoken by the witness, yes or no. And an agreement between the parties would do. If there's any dispute, we'll hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll do that, Mr. President. And that page may be reflected in the excerpts we seek to tender, depending on the outcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that if the accuracy issue has been resolved that you make it part of the excerpt. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, you discussed a moment ago whether members of your brigades attended meetings of the Crisis Staff. You opined whether it was obligatory for them to be on the Crisis Staff. Is it correct that by this point your recollection is refreshed as to whether Crisis Staffs existed in the municipalities in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, you sometimes attended Crisis Staff meetings yourself, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were not Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have --

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If -- please allow me to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've answered my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, witness. Witness. Witness. Witness, I'll stop you there. If --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are interrupting me all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I'm interrupting you and for good reasons, Mr. Boric. If you've answered the question that you do not know a certain thing and you say that these are not Crisis Staffs, that is accepted by Mr. Traldi as an answer to his question, and he may then put his next question to you. He is entitled to do that. So please do not again say that you should not be interrupted. If you're interrupted unfairly, I'll intervene -- witness. Witness. Witness, if you're talking about interrupting, that's what you're doing at this moment yourself. If the interruption would be unfair to you, I'll intervene. If, at the end of your testimony there's something you would like to add or say this where I was interrupted is important and I still want to bring it to your attention, you'll have an opportunity to do so. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 08917.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: These are the minutes of the 23rd Session of the Petrovac Municipality Crisis Staff. At the top, we see a list of persons present. The next-to-last name is Colonel Boric, Commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps. You did, in fact, have occasion to attend Crisis Staff meetings yourself, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably I attended that meeting. Had I known that -- or, rather, that I knew that that was called the Crisis Staff, I really had no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 08917 receives number P7333.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence; P7333. Witness, you've told us now quite a few things, including that you may have attended this meeting of the Crisis Staff. You told us that other meetings may not have been meetings of Crisis Staffs. Yesterday you said you weren't aware of the existence of a Crisis Staff or Crisis Staffs. That clearly contradicts, and I would ask you to be very precise in both listening to the question and in your answers. Because from today's testimony, it appears that you were aware of the existence of Crisis Staffs. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, aside from co-operating with the civilian authorities, the brigades in your corps also co-operated with the civilian police; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the chief of police would also be on the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32422, page 235. 32422, and this again is the OTP interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll try to get the P number right next time. Thank you, Your Honour. Page 235.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now at the very bottom of the page, you were asked: "... not only is a brigade commander is a member of the Crisis Staff, but in the municipalities, the chief of police or his designate is also a member of the Crisis Staff or War Presidency?" Turning to the top of the next page, we read your answer: "It was the chief of police who was usually -- not usually but had to be," we read "opt Crisis Staff." Do you stand by your portion of your interview as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see that the president of the municipality Novakovic invited me to a meeting. And at that meeting there were all of his co-workers. Now what their name was, were they a Crisis Staff --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... witness, I interrupt you again. A portion was read to you from what you said during the interview; that is, about the chief of police and his relation with the Crisis Staff. Do you stand by what you said then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Maybe he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's still not an answer to my question, but let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the bottom of this page --

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question was whether the chief of police was on the Crisis Staff. And I said that I did not know, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'm interrupting you again. That was not the question I put to you and listen carefully to the next question that will be put to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Continuing with the topic of co-operation between the brigades in your corps and the police, the bottom of the page you were asked about that co-operation. You were asked: "That's left to the local commanders dealing with their local SJBs then?" And you answer: "Yes. That's exactly right because, for instance, in Petrovac the brigade commander is in direct" -- and we turn to the next page: "... connection -- direct communication with local chief of the MUP in his zone." Do you stand by that answer that you provided as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say to that your recollection of events was fresher in 2004 than it is today?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to when Kljuc entered your area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P5137.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is your organisational order for the formation of the units of the 2nd Krajina Corps dated the 2nd of June, 1992. Turning to page 7 in the English and 6 in the B/C/S, at point 12, we see a reference to the 17th Kljuc Brigade. So it's clear that as of the 2nd of June, 1992, you were at the very least ordering the formation of a brigade in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Krajina Corps received an order from the Main Staff on the 3rd of July, 1992 to have the 17th Kljuc Brigade become part of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Now what you asked just now, I presume that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm putting to you that this, in fact, happened in early June 1992. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm waiting to read this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see here your order of the 2nd of June. Let's have 65 ter 31853 next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If the witness is still looking at the document, he should be allowed to finish what he wishes to read. Although it's mainly about the date, Mr. Boric, that Mr. Traldi asks you questions. Perhaps if we move to the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you see in the top left corner that the date is the 2nd of June?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 31853.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a daily combat report from the 17th Kljuc Light Infantry Brigade Command to the 2nd Krajina Corps Command dated the 12th of June, 1992. Does this refresh your recollection that by the 12th of June, 1992, the 17th Brigade was part of the composition of your corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the dates, but I also know the date when we received this, about the establishment of the brigade. You have that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 31854.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a daily combat report from the 17th Brigade the next day, the 13th of June, 1992. I'll ask again: Does this refresh your recollection that no later than the 12th and 13th of June, 1992, the 17th Brigade was part of your -- of the composition of your corps and sending daily reports to your corps command?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is written here is probably correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31853 and 31854.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 31853 receives number P7334. And 31854 receives number P7335.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7334 and P7335 are admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 06206.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an order for further operations from you, dated the 8th of June, 1992. Directing your attention to point 2 first, we read: "The Army of the SRBH has been given the task of offensive operations with the limited aim of repairing the operative-tactic position in the wider region of Sarajevo, in northern and Eastern Bosnia, while at the same time firmly holding the front lines on Serbian peripheral territories and protecting the Serbian people [sic] from genocide and extinction." This is an example of what we talked about before you issuing an order on the basis of a directive from the VRS Main Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in this case, that's Directive 1. For the record, P474. Turning to page 2 in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I think you read the -- "protecting the Serbian people." Whereas the original reads "the Serbian population."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. My notes may have been inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2, under point 4, we see that one of the things you've decided with a part of the force to control the area and liquidate splintered forces Green Berets in the municipality of Kljuc. This is because, as of the time you issued this order on 8th of June, Kljuc was in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see that here. Over here. On this slide.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If you look under the word "operaciju izvesti" and you look at the first point third line, you see a reference to Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you also see one at the top of the page; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you're issuing tasks regarding activities in Kljuc municipality in this order because by this point, it's part of your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turn to page 5 in both languages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a real answer to your question. We see that it's written, Witness. Is it accurate, what Mr. Traldi said, that this was within your area of responsibility on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I assume it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is why I'm saying -- may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I think you have responded by saying that you assume that it is. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At the bottom of this page in the English, and the top in the B/C/S, we read that prisoners take in these operations are to be transported to the 2nd Krajina Corps prisoner of war camp in the elementary school in the village of Kamenica, Drvar. That's the camp you mentioned yesterday which was under the control of the 2nd Krajina Corps's security organ; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a prison, but, all right, they called it a camp too. Camp is a bit broader. One always means Jasenovac, and there was no such thing. It is correct. There was a prison in Kamenica and Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm not necessarily comparing it to Jasenovac, sir. But we see in this document that you call it a camp; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the commander at Kamenica was subordinated to Major Mitrovic; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Major Mitrovic was the chief of security, and he was subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you say "chief of security." That's the chief of security in the 2nd Krajina Corps subordinated directly to you; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it would be the military police responsible for prisoners taken to the camp; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'd tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 06206 receives number P7336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7336 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, may be my mastering of the English language, but did you intend to say that the military police was responsible for the prisoners to be taken to the camps so, that is, transporting them to the camp or that they were responsible for prisoners that were taken to the camp and therefore were in the camp? But it may be that my understanding of the English language is not very precise in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I suspect that it -- on this occasion it's that my use of the English language may not have been very precise. Let me split the question up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, first, sir, it would have been the responsibility of the military police to transport the prisoners to the camp in Kamenica; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The subordinate units which had prisoners brought them to Drvar where the prisoners were taken over by the police. They would screen them and send them onto Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And prisoners held at Kamenica, they were under the responsibility of the military police, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now can we have P3754.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is an order for further operations dated the 25th of June, 1992 by Drago Samardzija, the commander of the 17th Brigade. He issued this order pursuant to your order that we just saw now, P7336; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see in point 1, he has decided to act jointly with the 6th Infantry Brigade. That's the 1st Krajina Corps unit at the time; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The commander of the 1st Krajina Corps at the time was General Momir Talic; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And because this operation involved units from both corps, you had to co-ordinate with General Talic about it; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The witness needs to repeat the answer because of the quality of sound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because of the quality of sound - and we hope that it is better, could you again complete your answer. The question was because this operation involved units from both corps, you had to co-ordinate with General Talic about it; right? And your answer was: No. Could you tell us what you then added.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the brigade commands co-ordinated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So your evidence today is you wouldn't have had to reach out to General Talic to co-ordinate this operation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Colonel Basara --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the answer. No, it is not right; no, I did not co-ordinate?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your answer is no, you didn't co-ordinate with General Talic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Colonel Basara, the commander of the 6th Brigade, would have reported to General Talic on the operation, while Colonel Samardzija would have reported to you; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, if we could have P7331, page 270. This will be another portion of your interview. As it comes up, you and General Talic would both report to General Mladic about this operation; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We reported about everything what happened in the 2nd Krajina Corps that day. Not only about that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you'd been shown this same document and here at line 12, you were asked: "Okay. Would you have to co-ordinate with General Talic for this particular operation?" And your answer was: "Yes. The representative of the 1st Krajina Corps which the corps had appointed the 6th Light Infantry Brigade, Light Brigade and the 1st Krajina Corps Command ordered the 6th Brigade to participate in this operation. And then -- and the commander of the 6th Brigade and Samardzija met and planned together this operation." Do you stand by that portion of your interview as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The part you just read out is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence in Colonel Samardzija's order that he ordered the mopping up of terrain including Hripavci and Krasulje. The Chamber has received evidence that two days later, the Kljuc SJB had a list of 103 persons who were detained mostly from Hripavci and Krasulje that were being held by the Kljuc police. The prisoners were immediately or the prisoners were first given over to the Kljuc police; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The document, the list by the Kljuc police, reflecting 103 prisoners that's P3755, the Chamber has received evidence - P218 - that 103 prisoners from Kljuc were then transported to Manjaca on the 27th of June, 1992. When you've said earlier in the your testimony that prisoners from the 2nd Krajina Corps would at times be transported to Banja Luka, you've been referring to Manjaca camp; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably to a place where they were grouped in Banja Luka. I don't know whether it was Manjaca or something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence, P220, that when the processing of those prisoners at Manjaca was completed, the 1st Krajina Corps's security organ was informed that processing prisoners from Kljuc was hard because: "They're being brought in massively and in large quantities. No selections that been made. They're bringing in those who shouldn't be treated as prisoners of war because they've been picked up from their homes and off their fields." Now that's what happened during these mopping-up operations by the 6th and 17th Brigades. People were picked up in their homes and on their fields and taken away to be treated as prisoners, even though there was no legal basis to do so; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There was a question, but Mr. Traldi will be happy to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What happened during these operations by the 6th and 17th brigades --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you have complained about being interrupted. Would you refrain from interrupting yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: What happened during these operations by the 6th and 17th Brigades is that people were picked up in their homes and on their fields and taken away to be treated as prisoners even though there was no legal basis to do so. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So prisoners taken by a brigade in your corps during operations you were aware of, you have no idea as you sit there today more than 20 years later whether there was any basis to hold them as prisoners; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn briefly to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P5186.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You testified yesterday at transcript page 34596 that you did not recall whether Bihac was declared a safe area. This is a letter from UNPROFOR to General Mladic expressing "grave concern at the extremely serious current situation in the SAFE AREA of BIHAC." Does this refresh your recollection as to whether Bihac was declared a safe area?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that it was declared a safe area because there was constant engagement from Bihac of the 2nd Krajina Corps. It was done from the 27th of June Barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you also not remember having allegations relayed to you of -- that your forces, 2nd Krajina Corps, were involved in "the unacceptable deliberate destruction of houses and the shelling of parts of Bihac city itself"?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to hear the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you remember having allegations relayed to you that your forces, the 2nd Krajina Corps, were involved in "the unacceptable deliberate destruction of houses and the shelling of parts of Bihac city itself"? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units at positions facing Bihac opened fire at those positions that they were fired from, from within the town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness. Witness, I'm -- have to interrupt you. The question was not what happened; but the question was whether you remember that allegations were relayed to you that this happened. So apart from whether it happened, but did you receive such allegations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was there, and I know what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to interrupt you. For the moment what I'm asking first is: We see this letter is sent to General Mladic. Were these allegations ever relayed to you by the Main Staff of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall having received a letter like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I'd put to you that your forces were, in fact, engaged in deliberate destruction of civilian houses in and around Bihac. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not. One cannot say that it was deliberate. It was a response to the fire coming from that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 03447.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a letter two days later. This time sent to President Karadzic. And I apologise we don't have a translation uploaded. We read here at the end of the first sentence about reports of deliberate and systematic targeting and destruction of civilian houses by Serb forces in the areas of Bosanska Krupa, Otoko, Dornja, Pokoj and Bihac. As of this time, the 3rd of March, 1994, those areas were within your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you did not, again, receive any information from the Main Staff that these allegations had been made to the Bosnian Serb leadership?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this document be marked for identification pending a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the number would be P7337.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7337 is marked for identification. Next time if you introduce a letter to a witness where there's no translation you should at least explain to the witness whose letter it was, addressed to whom, that is. But since the witness testified that there were no allegations, you said to whom it was addressed, but I don't think -- you say it was an UNPROFOR letter or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I didn't, and I'll make sure to next time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, as corps commander you agree you were responsible for the forces under your command; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, for instance, you received instructions from the Main Staff on the criteria for criminal punishment for soldiers; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Those instructions said, among other things, that if you don't properly deal with crimes by your subordinates, that crime is on their commander too; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The record does not show the witness's response to your previous question, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the commander finds about it and doesn't do anything about it, then correct -- it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the military courts and the military prosecution, those were under General Gvero's authority; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose it was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32447.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a dispatch from the Main Staff military prosecutor's office on the institution of criminal proceedings against persons who have not responded to the call-up or left units without authorisation. If we can have page 5 in the English and 3 in the B/C/S, we see General Gvero is issuing this to the military prosecutor's offices attached to the 1st Krajina Corps, the SRK, the IBK and the Herzegovina Corps. And we don't a mention of the military prosecutor's office attached to the 2 KK because, in fact, the 1st Krajina Corps military prosecutor's office had jurisdiction over the 2 KK; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. In the 2nd Krajina Corps, there was a lawyer who worked for the needs of the 1st Krajina Corps in terms of what was necessary regarding this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Gvero is directing that criminal proceedings be instituted against people not responding to the call-up because the military courts had jurisdiction over those subject to military obligations; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A number of your subordinates have been convicted of committing crimes against humanity and war crimes against non-Serbs during the war after the war in the courts of Bosnia-Herzegovina. You are aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. Who are those officers or soldiers?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you aware of Marko Adamovic's [sic] conviction for events at Biljani?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Ratko Dronjak's conviction, the commander of Kamenica camp?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the prisoner warden and I wasn't aware that he was sentenced. I know that there were proceedings instituted but I wasn't aware that there was a conviction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the Chamber has received the register of the Banja Luka military court, Exhibit P3563. It reflects that none of your subordinates were convicted for crimes against Muslims and Croats by the Banja Luka military court during the war. You're aware of that; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first I hear of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see it's a couple of minutes early but for continuity I would suggest that we break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could take a bit of an early break. Are you on track as far as time is concerned, Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think I can be a bit more accurate after the break. Mr. Stojanovic and I spoke this morning, and he'd asked that I reserve the last 30 minutes for him, and I'm making an effort to do so. I will organise myself during the break with that in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, an effort is always something. At least, we have to await the result but let's leave it to that. We'll take a break and we resume at 25 minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As usual, we'll start with verification of the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, Your Honour, everything is working fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Same is true for The Hague. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I start, my speed of speech may have been off but at temporary transcript page 35, I was recorded to inquire about Marko Adamovic, and I'd intended to inquire about Marko Samardzija, and I apologise for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you would put the question again to the witness so that he can answer. It's also in the new version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, just to complete the topic from before the break, are you aware of Marko Samardzija's conviction for events at Biljani?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am going to change topics now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P514.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is an order by General Mladic dated the 13th of April, 1994. At point 1 we see he orders in pertinent part that: "UN Military Observers and the members of UNPROFOR are to be accommodated in appropriate premises outside of the facilities where they had been stationed to date, that is, in the military facilities which are a potential target of the NATO air force as per your choice," and then he describes how they are to be secured. Turning to the end of the document in both languages, we see it's sent, among other things, to the command of the 2nd Krajina Corps. The Chamber has received evidence, P587, that three days earlier, Mladic had ordered the VRS to block UNPROFOR and humanitarian organisations' convoys and bring in and secure the personnel. Using detained people as human shields in this manner by "stationing them in potential targets of air-strikes" is not legal, is it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the area of the 2nd Krajina Corps, we did not have these men, and it is certainly not legal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you about it because you testified yesterday that in all your encounters with General Mladic, you never received an illegal order, either written or oral. Would you like now to correct that testimony?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And on that topic, that order we discussed yesterday that you sent implementing General Mladic's order to send soldiers on leave because they were Muslims or Croats -- were to send all soldiers who were Muslims and Croats on leave, adopting measures like that, purely on the basis of your subordinates' ethnicity, that wouldn't be legal either, would it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a war situation. I don't know whether it is legal or not, but if he wanted to preserve their lives, his manner of acting was excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Change topics again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see here on the left-hand side of the page in the B/C/S, the decision on the strategic objectives for the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm not going to go through them one by one, but can you just take a look for a moment and then confirm for us that you were aware of them during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a bit further.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is something you discussed in your interview. But how did you become aware of these objectives?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we had this briefing at the Main Staff, then I found out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who listed the strategic objectives at that briefing?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were written out, just like here, now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me ask slightly differently. Who provided the briefing on them?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, General Mladic and Mr. Karadzic were the main speakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And were the other corps commanders, as well as yourself, present for this?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And these strategic objectives were both military and political goals; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the political ones, but the military ones, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And General Mladic's orders would set out what your tasks were in order to realise the strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is Directive 4. Turning to page 4 in the English and page 9 in the B/C/S, I'd ask you to just take a minute to look at the tasks assigned to the 2nd Krajina Corps by this directive. It's on the lower part of the page in the B/C/S. And in its tasking to your corps, this directive implements the strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the strategic objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Which part?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, reaching the Una river.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's Objective 4, right, or part of Objective 4?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just like General Mladic is implementing the strategic objectives by issuing an operational directive to you, you would have implemented his directive by issuing an operational order to your subordinate brigades; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the 2nd Krajina Corps implemented Directive 4 by launching Operation Una-92; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, can we have page 5 in the English and 11 in the B/C/S, directing your attention to the Drina Corps's tasking, we see that the Drina Corps is to defend Visegrad, the dam, Zvornik and the corridor, the rest of its forces in the wider Podrinje region are to exhaust the enemy, inflict the heaviest possible losses on them and force them to leave the Birac, Zepa, and Gorazde areas with the Muslim population. Now, this -- this tasking also implements the strategic objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this task of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact, units of the 2nd Krajina Corps were deployed to the Podrinje area to assist the Drina Corps in implementing this task, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received evidence, P2242, that during those operations, the Drina Corps commander, General Zivanovic, informed your Chief of Staff, Colonel Vlaisavljevic, that he was in favour of continuing with the burning of Muslim houses during those operations in the Podrinje. I have two questions. First: Why was he -- why would he have been relaying that information if your units were not also taking part in the operations in that area?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that area, it did not participate. A unit participated in the area of Milici in order to protect the mine. Not in other areas though. When the defence of the Milici Brigade was threatened in the area of the mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Second question: Did Colonel Vlaisavljevic also relay to you the information about the destruction of Muslim property - the burning of their houses specifically - during these operations?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. We never talked about that. He never relayed that to me. I never heard of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finally on this topic, to return to the first question I'd asked you, I understand you testified you weren't familiar with this specific tasking. Based on your knowledge of the strategic objectives, however, you can tell that the tasking of the Drina Corps is also implementing those objectives; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't want to go into that now. I wouldn't want to give my opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're not asked about an opinion, but you were asked, based on your knowledge of the strategic objectives, whether you can tell that the tasking of the Drina Corps is also implementing these objectives. Was it or was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let us assume that that was the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we read, in pertinent part, in that tasking that the enemy forces are supposed to be forced to leave with the civilian population. Forcing the civilian population to leave, that's another illegal order; right.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You know, based on your training, that ordering subordinate forces to drive out the civilian population is illegal, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Misquote. Because the words used was -- were "drive out the civilian population." I would kindly ask my colleague to tell me where that is written in the document that we have before us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll phrase it very precisely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Forcing the Muslim population to leave an area, ordering your subordinate forces to do that is illegal; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of that order, and I cannot give my opinion whether Mladic did write that or did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the question, Witness. Could you tell us whether, according to your knowledge of international humanitarian law, as a professional -- professional officer, whether forcing the Muslim population to leave an area and ordering subordinate forces to do so, whether that is legal or illegal?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the speaker.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer. The interpreters did not catch your words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to international law, that is not legal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm done with this document, and I'm going to turn to the topic of prisoners held by your corps. Your corps had an exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps, Mr. Traldi, you again ask a question which you asked before, whether the witness would change his answer, that no illegal orders were issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'll give you another opportunity to change your answer as to whether General Mladic ever issued illegal orders. Would you like to change that testimony now?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never issued me an illegal order, and I wouldn't want to change anything in respect of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I'd like to take the witness back for a moment to the questions that were put to you in relation to the document in which orders were given that UN Military Observers and UNPROFOR members were to be put in places where, that is, stationing them in potential targets of air-strikes. You said: "That is not legal." But you added: "In the area of the 2nd Krajina Corps, we did not have these men." Now, I'd like to take you back. That order that UN Military Observers and UNPROFOR members were to be stationed in potential targets of air-strikes, that order, you said, was illegal. I have two questions. First: Were there any UN Military Observers and were there any UNPROFOR members in your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not stationed, but sometimes they --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat. You said they were not stationed but sometimes ... Could you resume from there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They would pass and go towards Bihac as announced, and we would see them off to the border of the zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So they were there from time to time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Passed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In order to pass, you have to be somewhere. My second question would be: Whether this order was addressed to the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is what is written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any reason to doubt that it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Why would I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that you were issued an order in rather general terms which, under circumstances, could have been implemented, you received an order which was illegal. I do not understand at this moment why you would not correct your testimony that you never received an illegal order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One needs to bear in mind what the reason behind it was, what the reason for writing it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it make -- does that make it any less illegal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would say that stationing UNPROFOR and UN Military Observers in locations which are potential targets of air-strikes would become illegal [sic] if you had a good reason for that? Would become any less illegal is, I think, what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose they were stationed with the forces of the VRS. So they were not separated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't my --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The goal was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That wasn't my question. The order clearly was to station them in potential targets of air-strikes and whether there would be any VRS members in that area or not, is that relevant for the illegality of that order.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had no problem with that. I did not implement the order, and I am not going to change what I had said previously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you were not asked whether you implemented any illegal orders. You were asked whether you received any illegal orders. Focussing on that, you would still not correct your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With regard to this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that we are talking about this issue. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to prisoners. Your corps had an exchange commission; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was led by an officer named Milan Ivancevic, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Under which organ of your corps did the exchange commission fall?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The political organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Is that legal, morale and religious affairs?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when your corps entered into an exchange agreement, the Main Staff had to approve that; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Main Staff was informed that there would be an exchange.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's have 65 ter 32428.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a document you issued the 13th of November, 1994 to the Main Staff. What we see here as the English comes up is that you're seeking -- you're urgently requesting the Main Staff's approval to enter into negotiations about an exchange; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And that's because you needed the Main Staff's approval to do so; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 32428.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were aware that some of the prisoners held by your brigades were taken to do forced labour at the front lines; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 19091.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a daily combat report from the Command of the 11th Brigade sent to the Command of the 2nd Krajina Corps dated the 1st of July, 1992. And we see at the end of point 1 that a captured enemy soldier had managed to escape while working on the entrenchment as what is described as "our forward line of defence." So you were, in fact, informed by your subordinate units that they sent prisoners to do forced labour at the front lines; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If one looks at this, it seems to be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7339.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Witness, you initially answered that you were not aware that some of the prisoners held by your brigade were taken to do forced labour. If we find elements in combat reports that this was the case, I would urge you to be very clear in telling us whether you were not aware of it but that it may have happened or that you were aware that it did not happen. Could you specify in any future answer which is the case, because it happened now a couple of times that looking at documents, we get answers which are not exactly consistent with your initial answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to focus now on Kamenica which we discussed earlier. Now Kamenica camp was just a beat-up old school with a barbed wire fence around it; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand from your interview that you claim you never visited Kamenica yourself; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I understand you claim that you never asked anyone what was going on there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a prison. There was no need. The security organ was competent and controlled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
