utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that you on at least one occasion issued an order regarding the treatment of prisoners of war. That's because you were responsible for the treatment of prisoners of war in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P3996.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a report issued by your assistant commander for information, Mladen Skenderija, on 5th of August. We see that, in accordance with the London Agreement, he is writing that an International Red Cross team and foreign journalists are visiting POW camps. The visits are conducted by organisations of the government and the team will be escorted by a representative of the army, a Lieutenant-Colonel Savo Sokanovic and refers to a prisoner-of-war camp in Drvar. Now that refers to Kamenica; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, while this bears Colonel Skenderija's name, of course, the potential visit to Kamenica camp would have been discussed in the corps command; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So is it your evidence today -- well, sorry. Let me start that question again. As a matter of course, an event like this would have been discussed in the corps command, including with you; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We did not discuss it. It was not on the agenda. It was done by the morale organ. It was Colonel Skenderija at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Kamenica --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... for a moment, sir. I'll ask you questions about the nature of Kamenica in a minute. If you were informed by a member of your corps command you were aware that a foreign journalist team, International Red Cross team might visit a camp in your area of responsibility under your corps's security organ, is it your evidence that under those circumstances you wouldn't have asked, What are they going to find if they go there?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably would.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you never heard reports that people were abused or killed there in your evidence; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never informed and I never heard that anyone was killed in Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32448.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this time we don't have a translation into English yet. If we can turn to the top of page 2 in the B/C/S, and this is a report coming from the 1st Krajina Corps intelligence and security organ to the VRS Main Staff dated the 5th of November, 1994. Here at the top of page 2, do you agree with me that we see in the first -- after the first hyphen, a report that Ratko Dronjak in Kamenica and Drvar took out seven people at night, and they were never seen again; is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that? Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could you just read slowly beginning at the word "osoba" for us.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just so we all have the exact text, can you read it aloud, please.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "A person from the Red Cross says that Ratko Dronjak was in Kamenica camp in Drvar and killed seven people from Vojic near Kljuc during one night and drove away with them in an unknown direction."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We didn't hear the very last words of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat the very last words, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Never heard of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you were never ordered to investigate it, could you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we first have the complete answer. Or was that -- were those the last words that you read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. "Never heard of this case." Were you reading the last few words, or were you commenting on what has happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is my comment. I am not familiar with this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I -- I do understand that. But you were invited to read the last few words again from the paragraph Mr. Traldi invited you to read because the last few words were not caught by the interpreters. So could you perhaps resume from where you said: "...during one night and drove away with them in an unknown direction," and what then follows? Would you please read that aloud for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "And he drove away with them in an unknown direction."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say you've never heard of that so you were never clearly ordered to investigate it; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 32448 receives number P7340.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32455.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for that document, I would have one additional question for you, Witness. The previous document we looked at, I don't know whether you remember which one it was. Otherwise I'll ... that was the document in which possible visits of the Red Cross were announced. Do you remember that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, were there any women and/or children kept in conditions which would be similar to being detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you have any explanation as why there was any concern that these visits would be exploited and that a special focus would be on women and children which suggests that at least women and children must have been in places where the Red Cross would visit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wasn't concerned with the Red Cross coming to visit the prison in Kamenica. I was actually glad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the document written by one of your subordinates expressed concern about those visits to be exploited and abused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not register who the person who expressed this concern was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the document was -- and -- was -- is signed by or at least is issued by Colonel Mladen Skenderija. You had a look at it a second ago. If need be, we can go back to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You'd like to go back to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yeah -- well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Concern is expressed there that, especially in relation to women and children, that the visits might be exploited. Do you have any explanation for that, if you were not aware in any way that women and children were kept in conditions similar to detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time I hear about that, from you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is the Trial Judgement in Ratko Dronjak's case, the warden. And if we can turn to page 45 in B/C/S and 13 in the English which represents just the parts we've had translated. We see a section headed, "Non-contentious facts." And if we could turn to page 15 in the English, 47 in the B/C/S, paragraph 206, we read, based on Ratko Dronjak's testimony, that your corps's exchange commission headed by Milan Ivancevic was directly linked to the prison and knew who was inside at any time. So is it your evidence, as you've just told the Presiding Judge, that you'd never heard about the types of people who were being held there even though your subordinates on the exchange commission knew?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 21 in the English, 57 in the B/C/S we read in paragraph 246 that a witness named Dragan Rodic who, as other evidence in the judgement or portions of the judgement reflect, was a shift commander at Kamenica who pled guilty that he stated that the detained civilians were detained solely for the fact that they were not Serbs. Did you ever ask any of your subordinates in the security organ why the people at Kamenica were being detained there?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not ask. Because I was not involved in it. I was at the front line taking care of defending our area of responsibility. I didn't ask it of anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your command post was in Drvar; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, but it was in Ostrelj, between Drvar and Petrovac most of the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Kamenica is also in Drvar; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: About how far apart were they?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think 2 or 3 kilometres. Not more. It is near Drvar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, when you said a moment ago you were at the front line taking care of defending our area of responsibility, in fact, you were no more than 2 or 3 kilometres away from the camp; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in Drvar at first but then we moved to Ostrelj rather soon afterwards which is much further away.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 4 of this judgement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi before we continue I object to the way you -- you presented the evidence of the witness where you said that he had answered my question, that he never heard about the types of people who were being held. Because I only asked about women and children. And since the follow-up of your question is about civilians that could include men as well, so that is not fair to the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take the point, Your Honour. Can we have page 4 in both languages, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to focus on section 2 of the judgement. This refers in paragraphs 2 -- sorry, paragraphs 1 and 2, subparagraphs 1 and 2, to persons who were killed or who were detained there and then killed. And I'm just going ask to you focus on three names. Under point 2.1, Kalmin Kalic and Enver Cehic. And under 2.2, Kemal Sepic. Do you see those names?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32449.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is the Bihac cantonal court report on the exhumation, autopsy, and identification of bodies from the mass grave Jama Golubnjaca in Drvar and the report then refers to 19 male bodies that were found, of which three were identified. I see we're waiting to release ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, there's no English translation uploaded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, do you have an English translation before I ask whether you uploaded it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We do. And we've uploaded it, and we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it's released soon?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: While it comes up, sir, we'd discussed -- yesterday on direct you testified that the army had nothing to do with the departure of civilians from your area of responsibility. Is it your evidence that the detention of civilians in these conditions at Kamenica, just because they were not Serbs, had nothing to do with their departure from the 2nd Krajina Corps' area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Your Honours, apparently I had misspoken a moment ago and we don't have the translation. I'd looked at the screen and seen something that apparently was not what I thought I was looking at. But, sir, I can tell you that in this report, in this exhumation report, we'll see again the names of Kalmin Kalic, Enver Cehic, Kemal Sepic are you aware that people detained at Kamenica have been, after the war, exhumed from mass graves also in area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since we have the B/C/S version on the screen you could direct the attention of the witness to that portion of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll do so in a moment but I'd ask for an answer to my question.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Are you aware that people detained at Kamenica have been, after the war, exhumed from mass graves in your area of responsibility. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay. And I'll return -- my notes are incomplete as to the page numbers but we've just fixed that. Can we have page 4. And we see at the bottom of the page, number 3, Kemal Sepic. Turning to page 5, we see at name 8, Enver Cehic; and name 15, Kalmin Kalic. So the truth is people detained in your corps' camps were exhumed from mass graves in your area of responsibility after the war; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe they were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 01060.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, Major Mitrovic, Ratko Dronjak's superior, was promoted to lieutenant-colonel by General Mladic in January 1993; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7341.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we have 65 ter 32432.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what we see here dated the 12th of October, 1992 is a certification by General Mladic that you had also been promoted; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was promoted on the 16th of December, 1992. I was promoted to the rank of Major-General.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I tender 65 ter 32432.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number P7342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7342 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, that completes my questions about Kamenica --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you would wait for a second, witness. This completes Kamenica, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And regarding any portions of the judgement or the exhumation report, I'll speak with Mr. Stojanovic and see if there are any matters in dispute. We've uploaded other proof of death materials for the victims I mentioned but I anticipate it won't be necessary to tender all of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in view of the evidence of the witness that they may have been exchanged, are there autopsy reports indicating cause of death?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'd have to go through them and I'll do so at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Witness, you wanted to add something. You have an opportunity to do so now. If it is relevant as an answer to one of the questions that was put to you. So not to raise any issues that you consider to be interesting but in direct relation to questions that you were put to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading this certificate and it is written here that I'm being promoted --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The sound has gone bad again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, we have some problems with the quality of the sound. Could you -- if you were reading from the document or drawing our attention to parts of it, could you do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written here is certificate, concerning my promotion in the month of October. A general is promoted to that rank by the Supreme Commander by way of a decree and I received that decree on 16th of December, 1992. The decree promoting me to the rank of Major-General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think most important is that you were promoted rather than exactly -- the exact date of it. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn back to Kljuc municipality now, sir. And along with the 17th Brigade, you had an engineering regiment, the 2nd Engineering Regiment, based at Laniste in Kljuc municipality; right.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That regiment answered directly to you in the corps Command Staff so that the 17th Brigade's commander would have to call you to request assistance from the unit; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the way it's supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's the way it was; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which case you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In principle, the brigade commander in Kljuc had to call the corps command to request assistance from the 2nd Engineering Regiment; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the engineering regiment had standard engineering equipment: Bulldozers, excavators, that type of equipment; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P520. And I'm going to turn to Biljani now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is an order by Colonel Drago Samardzija dated the 9th of July, 1992. At that point he was the commander of the 17th Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Directing your attention to point 2a, assignments for units, we read that this operation is going to be carried out by the 2nd Battalion of the 17th Brigade reinforced with the reconnaissance platoon, a military police squad, and a police platoon. And we see above that it will start at 0500 hours on the 10th of July. Now you were aware of that operation; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter 32422 -- sorry P7331. Page 272.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now we see you're shown this order dated the 9th of July. We see you read it out. Refers to operations 0500 hours on the 10th of July, 1992. If we could scroll down, we see you're asked: "This is an operation that you would be monitoring? And you answer: "Yes." And if we turn to the next page, the beginning of your answer is recorded as indiscernible but you say definitely with the knowledge of the corps command. You're asked: "Samardzija is not just going to plan an order and just do it without letting you know, is he?" And you say: "Correct." Now, first, do you stand by those portions of your OTP interview in 2004 as truthful and accurate?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have page 276.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, does the witness not remember that he stands by this?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, do I understand your answer to mean whether you no longer remember that the portions I read back to you are accurate. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that I had said that. I see this in a foreign language and you're just reading that, and that does not have to be correct necessarily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, if you say that's not what I said, then we'll verify on the basis of the audio whether the recording is accurate, yes or no. If you say, I don't remember, then it leaves it open whether you said it or not. But if you say, I definitely did not say this, then we'll have it verified. What is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't remember. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I leave it to the Defence whether they will insist with the Prosecution on further verification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have page 276 of your interview for the moment and I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I add one sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If one line is indiscernible which may really affect the meaning of that sentence, then I think you should have excluded that from asking the witness whether he stands by it or not because depending what is indiscernible it could be anything. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Beginning at line 16 -- actually, let's start just above that. Line 12, you're being asked about the same order. You say that, "Colonel Samardzija sent it to his subordinate units. He sent that to his units. He didn't send that to me. I never saw this because he had received a task according to that decision from me, and then he devises his own order." So first question: Clearly at the time you recalled enough to opine on the process of who this order was communicated to; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly wasn't sent to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you stand today by your statement in the interview that he issued this order based on a task he'd received from you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below that we see you're asked: "Are you monitoring his combat operations on the 10th of July, 1992? What if he needs help?" And you answer: "My Chief of Staff was monitoring at this time." Now does that refresh your recollection as to whether you were aware of the operation that Colonel Samardzija had ordered?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not monitoring that operation. Maybe - I don't remember - the Chief of Staff was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall saying that in your interview, that your Chief of Staff, Colonel Vlaisavljevic, was monitoring the operation?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 277.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now here you mention Colonel Vlaisavljevic, your Chief of Staff. You were asked where he was on the 10th of July, 1992. You say you think he was at Laniste. You say there was a barracks in Laniste. You were asked if there's a barracks in Laniste, correct? You say: Yes, the commander of the 2nd Engineering Regiment. You say -- you were asked well, he had coms with you, he had communications with you, when necessary. And you answer yes. Do you stand today by your statements in your interview that Colonel Vlaisavljevic was present in Laniste during the operation Colonel Samardzija ordered in the document we just saw and had communications with you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have 65 ter -- sorry. Can we have the same document, page 281. And we see -- sorry, this page may be inaccurate in my notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let me just ask the question. After this operation was completed, the operation in Biljani, do you recall being told that it had been successful?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's scroll down to the bottom of the page, Mr. Grady asks you: "Now, general, I want to know what you were told on the 10th of July, 1992, about what happened in Biljani in the municipality of Kljuc during Samardzija's combat operation." You respond: "Just that the task was carried out and that the territory had been liberated." Does that refresh your recollection as to, first, whether you were aware of this operation; and, second, whether you were told it had been carried out successfully?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was no operation. That was a tactical task. Probably what I said then is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So we agree you were aware of this tactical task as it was being carried out; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have page 275 of the same interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you had been shown the tasking of the Sanica police platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. GRADY SAYS
utterances.text: "So again, this is another situation where the Kljuc SJB is involved in a combat operation." And you respond: "It's placed under the command of the brigade commander, yes." Do you stand today by your statement at the time that the Kljuc SJB was under the command of Brigade Commander Samardzija during this operation?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber has received evidence from a number of witnesses that well over 100 people detained at the Biljani school were murdered on or about the 10th of July, 1992. You're aware of that today as you sit there; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This Chamber has received evidence from a Defence witness, named Nikola Vracar that the massacre was the talk of the town. The Chamber has received evidence from a witness named Bertie Weiss that Marko Samardzija told him he had contacted his commander among others to tell him what was about to happen. It's your evidence that it was the talk of the town in your area of responsibility during an operation you were aware of that your Chief of Staff with whom you had a good relationship as you testified early was monitoring and in the last 23 years, you yourself have not become aware of this massacre. Is that your evidence today?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The sound has gone bad again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your answer because the quality of the sound was bad.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, the question was whether you know it now, not whether you knew it then, but whether you know it now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know it now either.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has also received evidence that the people killed were exhumed from a site less than a kilometre from the Laniste barracks where that engineering regiment that answered to your corps was based. It's your evidence that you were not aware of the mass burial of the victims of this massacre.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: An operation like that would have required that engineering regiment to use resources, use its vehicles, use gasoline; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That would have been reflected in reports it was sending to the logistics organ of the corps, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that was not in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you weren't aware of this massacre that was the talk of the town but you're testifying today that you're confident that the reports the engineering regiment send up did not reflect increased activity during the period when these victims would haven buried. Have I understood your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I put to you your evidence about this is not credible and you could not have avoided knowing about this massacre committed by your soldiers and others subordinated to them during it. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is your opinion. You're entitled to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know we are on a slightly unusual schedule today, or slightly different than normal. I think we're close to the time for the break. I have a relatively brief period remaining for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what is a relatively brief period?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Certainly no more than ten minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No more than ten minutes. Then we'll take the break now. We'll resume at 25 minutes past 1.00. And then, Mr. Stojanovic, the remaining time is, as you have discussed it with Mr. Traldi; at least there's a little bit more perhaps for any final questions by Mr. Traldi. We take the break. Witness, we'd like to see you back in half an hour. We take a break, and we resume at 25 minutes past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We check again whether the videolink is functioning well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Via videolink] Yes, it is, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just briefly to provide the Chamber the information it had requested before the break, the information as to cause of death is actually in the exhumation report that I used and attributes for all of the individuals violent deaths, says almost all in civilian clothes, with two wearing items of clothing that may be considered as military garb. Those two are not any of the three I referred to by name. It also saying that some of the individuals were blindfolded and doesn't identify those by name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, and they were -- the mass grave was in the territory controlled by Republika Srpska or is that, just a location. I invite the parties to agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just so we understand what we're being asked to agree on, at what time in history?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of the exhumation or of the war?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relevance of the question may be to fully appreciate the suggestion - it wasn't more than that - by the witness that it may have been that they had been exchanged, which would make it unlikely that if they died after that, they would then nevertheless be found in a mass grave which is located not then in Federation-controlled area. I mean, in order to assess the credibility of -- or the possibilities in that respect, it may be important to know whether the mass grave was in territory and controlled by whom at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I apologise for not immediately understanding that, Your Honour. Thank you for the clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I want to turn finally to the departure of Muslims from your area of responsibility, both Muslims and Croats. Now, you testified yesterday at transcript page 34592 that most of the non-Serbs had left before the creation of the 2nd Krajina Corps. In fact, you know thousands and thousands of non-Serbs left your area of responsibility during your time as corps commander; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with a figure --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The figure wasn't as high.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of them did leave though.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, for instance, you were aware of convoys of thousands of Muslims out of Kljuc municipality during your time as corps commander; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have P355, page 26, in the English and the B/C/S transcript. As it comes up, this will be one of General Mladic's notebooks from the war. These are a portion of his notes of a meeting he attended on the 11th of September, 1992. We see the president of Jovo Banjac -- sorry the president of Kljuc municipality, Jovo Banjac's name. We see that. Mladic records him as giving thanks to the 30th KD commander and Colonel Vlaisavljevic. That's your Chief of Staff; right.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see that Mr. Banjac is recorded as informing General Mladic there were 17.000 Muslims and now there are 5.000. And 1500 left today. Like General Mladic you were aware that more than a thousand Muslims left Kljuc in September 1992, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P356, page 123 in the English and the B/C/S transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be another of General Mladic's notebooks from the war, and we're going to see an entry on the 4th of November, 1992, 1800 hours, a meeting with the representatives of the authorities of Petrovac, Drvar, Kljuc. If we turn to page 125, we'll see references to Colonel Vlaisavljevic and to you. You and your Chief of Staff both attended this meeting; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning back to page 124, we see at the bottom Vinko Kondic from the MUP in Kljuc is recorded to say that: "About 2.000 Muslims are now living in Kljuc municipality, and there used to be 17,5." It's a reference again to there used to be being 17.000 or more than 17.000 Muslims in Kljuc municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so we see here you and General Mladic together meeting this time with the civilian police chief and being informed of the massive exodus of Muslims from Kljuc, one of the municipalities in your area of responsibility; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that means from the beginning of the conflict in all likelihood, not as of the moment when the corps was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you attended meetings of the Una-Sana region, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In June 1992.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have D1027, MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now this is a record of the second inter-municipality talks at Korcanica on 14th June 1992. At number 19 on this list, we see you; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My name can be found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you attended this meeting, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you tell me the date?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: 14th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you remember you attended at least some meetings of this regional group; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I attended several meetings, but I don't know what their names were or what groups were there and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the Chamber has received evidence that at the previous meeting, this group took the position that Muslims and Croats had to be moved out of their regions until their population was reduced to a level where Serb authority could be maintained. A previous meeting on 7 June 1992 after the creation of your corps. Now, you were aware that there were discussions and efforts to reduces the Muslim population of municipalities in your area of responsibility during your time as corps commander; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The Chamber has received evidence, P3853, that as of early 1995, the Banja Luka CSB was a ware that in every municipality in your area of responsibility, including the ones that had been majority Muslim before the war, the population had become at least 93 per cent Serb. You were aware of that too, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that percentage.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're certainly aware that the ethnic composition of the population in the municipalities in your area of responsibility was overwhelmingly Serb by the end of your time as corps commander; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you testified yesterday that the VRS didn't have anything to do with it and you didn't think there were any situations where the front line had to be opened to facilitate an exchange of population. To get, for instance, from Petrovac to Split on a convoy, someone would have to get through the front line; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: To get from Kljuc to Travnik, somebody would have to cross the front line; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That would require --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We did not hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the last thing you said, sir.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that politicians were supposed to reach agreement and the military would let them go through whatever route they were to take.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So now you do recall occasions when the VRS would open the front line to facilitate these exchanges.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not go through my area but they did go outside of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, may I remind you of your own words, certainly not more than ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That was approximately -- we started some 14, 15 minutes ago. Could you please wind up because Mr. Stojanovic, I think, you agreed that would you have half an hour and then it's --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you testified that the VRS didn't have anything to do with the people leaving. We've seen brigades under your command, we've seen evidence that they massacred civilians, rounded up people, destroyed civilian property. Those things had everything to do with the Muslim populations' flight from the municipalities in your area of responsibility, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any questions in re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, you were asked about your attendance at the meetings of civilian structures, and you were shown a document which concerns your attendance in -- at a meeting in the Petrovac municipality. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Court how did it come about that you would be in attendance at such a meeting?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal president would call me and say, We have a meeting. He wouldn't say meeting of a Crisis Staff but he said we have a meeting of the leadership. He would then ask me to come there and explain the situation at the front lines. That's how it went. Then he would state any needs on behalf of the population and what it was that we could do to help.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'll wait for the interpretation. Did you at any point in time receive written invitations to attend such meetings with an agenda?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was usually called on the phone or through direct contact, when we would encounter each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you invited to all municipal meetings or only those when military issues were on the agenda?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not invited to all meetings. I suppose I was invited when military issues were to be discussed or someone from the corps command would attend instead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned documents of the Main Staff of the VRS which speak to the establishment of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Next could we please have document P4381 in e-court. General, before you is a document dated the 4th of June, 1992, as we can see in the left upper corner. It comes from the Main Staff of the then-Army of the Serbian Republic of BiH. Kindly direct your attention at item 2, which is on the next page of the document, where it reads: "For the purposes of determining the boundaries of responsibilities in the areas between corps, I hereby set corps' area of responsibility as follows ..." And then we have the 1st Krajina Corps, and at b, the 2nd Krajina Corps, detailing its zone of responsibility. Is this the document which dealt with the issue of place, position, and zone of responsibility of the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of these locations are within the zone, but there is another document which details the municipalities in order to define the zone. These are just some of the geographic locations inside the zone. Some of them do ring a bell, whereas others do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. As the corps commander, did you caution an order -- issue orders to the effect of how to treat POWs and that rules regulating their status should be observed?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. A course was also set up by representatives of the Red Cross to that effect. Brigade commanders and their assistants for morale were present where they were familiarized with the Geneva Convention pertaining to the treatment of POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As the corps commander, did you insist on honouring the regulation in terms of treating POWs by those in your subordinate units?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We pointed that out in our orders, stating that they should abide by those rules and that they should respect the prisoners and their rights. The procedure in case of capture was also described. That is what we acquainted everyone with.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we next have P39 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you can wait for one second since the document is still on our screen. Witness, you told us that this document, especially under b where the 2nd Krajina Corps is -- is mentioned, just give geographical locations within the zone of the -- of responsibility. However, the document says that these are the boundaries. Do you have any explanation as why you consider this just a handful of locations within the zone of responsibility instead of what the document says, these being boundaries?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see that these are boundaries, such as Celebici and the Korcine Pass and Malovan, Setac [phoen].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you referred to another document, could you tell us what that document is where you said the municipalities, I think, are mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be found where the order on establishment of the 2nd Krajina Corps was. It details the units and the zone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Stojanovic, perhaps my recollection is not -- not -- not that well. Is that a document we have looked at already or are you going to tender that since the witness relies on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think we have seen that document. During my re-direct, I will show another document to the witness which might be the one he referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that in proofing you would have verified that, this apparently being an important issue, but please proceed. We'll hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we next have P3995, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, this document bears your name. The date is the 5th of August, 1992. The title: Order on treatment of prisoners of war. In item 2 of the document, we read: "It is forbidden, regardless of the circumstances, to treat a prisoner with cruelty. Prisoners must be treated humanely and must be protected from violence, verbal abuse and intimidation. Prisoners shall retain the full civic, legal and civil capacities that they had at the time of capture." Is this the document you referred to a moment ago, in terms of its formulation?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, did you, at any point in time, have information that some officers of your subordinate units acted in contravention of what is designated here?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During the examination, a man by the name of Ratko Dronjak was mentioned. While you were performing the duty of the commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps, did you ever have an opportunity to meet this member of the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he was warden of the prison in Kamenica. I've never seen him. I don't know him. I never went to visit the prison of Kamenica. That was under the security organs, the police, and that's what they did. And they also reported to the command about certain problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far away was the facility of Kamenica from Ostrelj, where you had your command post most of the time while you were commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, maybe I'll make a mistake, but, say, it's about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How long did POWs stay at this facility before they were sent to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For as long as the security organs needed to carry out their work and compile records of everything they did with them. And then with these records and reports, they would go to Banja Luka with the POWs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have document P4052 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While we're waiting for it, Mr. Stojanovic, you asked whether the document we just had on our screen was the document the witness referred to a bit earlier. He described - at least the last document I think he mentioned - it as the zone of responsibility defined by municipalities. I don't see any of that in the document you have just shown to us. So, therefore, if you had another document in mind, then you could address the matter as you wish, but I have difficulties in reconciling the last document the witness described with what you have shown us on the screen. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This document deals precisely with the topic that we've been discussing. I'm going to put some questions now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I was talking about the previous document which did not reflect what the witness earlier said. At least the last document he suggested that would exist. It doesn't reflect in any way with what he described then. But if it's the new one, well, I don't see that many municipalities at first sight, but I'll wait for your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, General, you have a document before you dated the 9th of June, 1992. In this document, the Command of the 30th PARTD is submitting to the Command of the 1st Krajina Corps an explanation about resubordination, and it says that in the building of the SO Kljuc a meeting was held with NS of the 2nd Krajina Corps who, on behalf of the Command of the 2nd Krajina Corps, informed the commander of the 30th PARTD that the territory of the SO Kljuc and the units deployed on that territory are being resubordinated to the Command of the 2nd Krajina Corps. Do you know anything about this meeting in which - as it seems here - the Chief of Staff took part, the Chief of Staff of the 2nd Krajina Corps, in an attempt to resolve the question of resubordinating the unit from Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- and that meeting was attended by the Chief of Staff, Colonel Mico Vlaisavljevic. In Kljuc, there was not a brigade. There were territorial units, and when Colonel Drago Samardzija arrived, he reported on the 9th of June, 1992, he was supposed to establish a brigade, the 17th Brigade, in Kljuc. After that, an order arrived from the Command of the Main Staff. That was the 3rd of July. Stating that in Kljuc, the establishment of the 17th Brigade, Light Infantry Brigade, should be made official.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness -- could you tell us what PARTD stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partisan Brigade, the 30th Partisan Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you really saying it's partisan brigade or partisan division because the D could also stand for division, as it is translated on top of that document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct. You're right. Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: During this transition period, who was in charge of equipping the unit from Kljuc logistically in terms of weapon, personnel, materiel?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since it was supposed to be established and become part of the 2nd Krajina Corps, all its needs had to be met by the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like us to take a look at a document together and its 65 ter number is 03067. General, sir, there is a document here of the War Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc dated the 13th of July, 1992, and it is signed by the president of the War Presidency, Jovo Banjac. It says that this is a conclusion, and you can read it. It's before you so I don't have to read everything. However, what indicates who it is that leads this unit and which does not correspond to what you've been saying right now, which is the way things should be according to rules and that's why I'm ask you all this so that you would explain it to the Court. In paragraph 4 it says that the Executive Board of the SDS Kljuc should make a list of officers and forward it to the brigade commander in order to reinforce the Command Staff of the brigade, mainly for morale, from battalion to brigade level. Do you know what this is all about, General, sir?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see Colonel Drago received an order to report to the duty on the 9th of June, 1992, and the Main Staff, as far as the establishment of the 2nd Krajina Corps is concerned, it was included on the 3rd of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could Mr. Stojanovic please turn off his microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So as far as manning the brigade is concerned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you're invited to switch off your microphone. Please continue your answer, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, let take a look at the document. P520.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You had the opportunity to see that document a moment ago. You remember this document, General, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at the second page. Could we zoom in on the stamp of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So this is an order for further action, and it's signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Samardzija. The date is the 9th of July, 1992. Now I'm asking you the following. Can you recognise this stamp and what does this stamp say?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the stamp of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc, and that proves that the -- at that time, the 17th Brigade had not been within the 2nd Krajina Corps yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to ask that document 65 ter -- actually, the one I showed a moment ago 03067 be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the document receives number D1032.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, can you tell the Chamber where that village is, Donji Biljani?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, you were trying to say something.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the territory of the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: How far away is that area from the place where your command post was?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say exactly now in terms of kilometres, but it's certainly more than some 30 kilometres to Kljuc. Maybe it's even more than that, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Today, now that you've seen these documents, do you still stand by that, namely, that in July, until the 13th of July, 1992, the unit from Kljuc still hadn't been fully subordinated to the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question, General, sir. The 30th Krajina Division that is mentioned in this document, the one that you had an opportunity to see a moment ago and whose commander is Colonel Stanislav Galic, was it at any point of time within the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. It was never within the 2nd Krajina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I should conclude with a few questions that have to do with Bihac. General, sir, you said at one moment that the fiercest intensity of fighting in your area of responsibility was at the Bihac front. Were there ever orders that were issued by the Main Staff or by you personally, as corps commander, to the subordinate units that targets in the town of Bihac and civilian settlements should be hit in a non-selective manner?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received such an order, and I never issued such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Was there such fighting and was there an exchange of artillery fire between the units of the 5th Corps and the 2nd Corps at the Bihac front?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As a soldier, how would you assess the intensity of that fighting at the Bihac front while you were commander of the 2nd Krajina Corps?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to explain this a bit to us in language that would be a bit more acceptable. What would that mean for you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we held this line towards Bihac practically 90 per cent of the time while the war was still on until the Muslims received assistance from the air and from the Croats, when they pushed us back. But after an offensive was launched, we returned to the next position, the one that we had held earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: General, sir, thank you for your answers, the answers that have you provided. We have no further questions for you. Thank you very much indeed?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. In view of one of the answers given by the witness and reading the stamp about which the witness was asked, which he said was the stamp of the -- of the Kljuc municipality, I think he said, could we have a -- the translation of that stamp being verified? Because I do, indeed, see Kljuc, opstina of Kljuc. At least in the English, I think it's in two languages, but I also see skupstina, which is perhaps not the same and I see the translation in English: "Km of the 17th Light Infantry Brigade" or is that ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, might I briefly address it with the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so. But briefly indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll have about five minutes total, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If interpreters and security, and all us assisting us, transcription, transcribers, then we are able to let the witness leave this week and not to return for five minutes next week. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we zoom in very tightly on the large word "Kljuc" just to the left of the centre of the stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the words "teritorijalne obrane" next to that word "Kljuc"?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It reads Municipal Assembly of Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the specific words I asked you, "teritorijalne obrane," which you're leaving out of what you're reading?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we zoom out slightly. That sometimes assists in ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the witness doesn't see the enlargement due to the videolink. But if -- Mr. Stojanovic, could you read in the -- or could you confirm that those words are in the stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I think I can read it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... if you would do so, then --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I can't see the first part but it says the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Then in the next smaller circle, Kljuc Municipal Assembly. And in the third circle: Municipal staff of the Territorial Defence. And then in large letters: Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, it was, in fact, the municipal staff of the Kljuc Territorial Defence that weeks, at least a month before this point, had, in fact, been transformed into the 17th Brigade; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It cannot be that the municipal staff was turned into a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Let's have 65 ter 32434.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps if you remind the witness that it was not the municipal staff but it's Territorial Defence which you were referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, the municipal Territorial Defence was, in fact, transformed into a brigade. That happened in Kljuc and Mrkonjic Grad, that you testified about during direct examination; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part of the Kljuc Territorial Defence was made part of the 17th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, what we see on our screen now is an order from yourself dated the 7th June 1992. If we turn to page 2 in both languages, we see the recipient list includes - already on the 7th of June, 1992 - the 17th Light Infantry Brigade in Kljuc. More than a month before the Biljani incident you had the ability to issue orders to the 17th Brigade, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was after the agreement between the Chief of Staff and the 30th -- commander of the 30th Partisan Brigade to establish the 17th Brigade which was to become part of the 2nd Krajina Corps. In order to do that, it took --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it took a while for the brigade to be formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this issue is -- this order is issued just one day after P4052 reflected that agreement. That agreement was implemented immediately and the brigade came under your command. That's the truth, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In your terms, the brigade is full and ready immediately to go to a theatre of war. Well, it doesn't work like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to make this quick. We see here you issued orders to the brigade more than a month before Biljani. We've seen they issued reports to you weeks before Biljani. You've described how Colonel Samardzija, in late June 1992, orders an operation in Kljuc pursuant to your order for offensive operations. What you're doing now is you are providing evidence that is not true about the chain of command of this brigade at the time of the Biljani incident to avoid your own responsibility for a massacre committed by soldiers under your command. That's the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: GRUJO BORIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. I'd tendered 65 ter 32434 and D1027 MFI, which I'd used at the end of cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, 32434 receives number P7343.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7343 is admitted into evidence. And then you said another one, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: D1027. That was the Una-Sana minutes, the 14 June minutes that I'd used late in cross and had neglected to tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the number -- it's a D exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It's MFI'd pending a decision and so I'd just ask that it be admitted at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and it was MFI'd because there was no translation at the --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It was MFI'd. It was one of a number of associated exhibits to Witness Erceg's evidence, and numbers were reserved and MFI'd pending a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection? If not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D1027 is now admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just the last document I'd ask that 65 ter 32449, the exhumation report, be MFI'd pending a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you are invited to see to what extent we could work with an excerpt because it was for a very specific purpose introduced. Madam Registrar, the number to be reserved for the exhumation report would be.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P7344.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Have we dealt with all of the exhibits? No further comments, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'd remained to talk about the judgement and whether any proof of proof-of-death documents were necessary, but we can do that at any time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Anything about the interview of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As already mentioned what is left is to see whether we can agree on the text of interview conducted by the OTP with this witness. That is for me and the Prosecutor to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you have no other problem than that, Mr. Traldi, would you give it some thought as to how that interview would fit within the 92 ter, 92 bis range because the witness did not attest to it. I don't know for what purposes, how you want to use that, but the Chamber would like to have that very clear, whether you would tender those excerpts for the truth of its content, where the witness has not attested to that truth. Therefore the Chamber would like to know exactly what we are -- what we will have to decide upon once you tender that excerpt.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Does the Chamber wish to hear at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, not at this moment. We are already at 30 minutes but perhaps you do that soon or make a short written submission about it. I leave it in your hands, but I take it that you are aware of how Rules 92 ter and 92 bis are to be applied and what possible consequences there are for this document. We -- first of all, Mr. Boric, we thank you very much for coming to the videolink room. We thank you also for having answered the questions put to you by the Bench, put to you by the parties, and I wish you a safe return home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can conclude the videolink. Then we adjourn for the day, and we'll resume Tuesday, the 28th of April, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I, but we'll not adjourn until after we have thanked very much all those who have assisted far beyond the usual time that is security, that is interpreters, that is transcribers, and all other staff who supported that. We stand adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 28th day of April, 2015, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.31 p.m.,
